rendered: The premise does not match the paper: the authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte with the sodium metal anode. They explicitly moved away from carbonates. As opposed to using traditional organic carbonate electrolytes[1], the coin cells were assembled using NaPF6 salts dissolved in tetraglyme as electrolyte[2][3]. The reason given is that this glyme electrolyte was chosen to overcome the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes[4][5] that was observed in carbonate-based electrolytes, and a stable sodium-anode interface is critical to good cycling performance. Building on earlier work, the authors relied on the sodium anode stability that glymes support during reversible plating. The glyme choice is also described as part of the strategy in the paper's introduction, where the cell is assembled with a glyme-based electrolyte.[6][7]
